extraction.name: MTEB: Massive Text Embedding Benchmark
extraction.description: The Massive Text Embedding Benchmark (MTEB) spans 8 embedding tasks covering a total of 58 datasets and 112 languages. Tasks include Bitext mining, classification, clustering, pair classification, reranking, retrieval, STS and summarization. Through the benchmarking of 33 models on MTEB, this establishes the most comprehensive benchmark of text embeddings to date.
extraction.creator: Niklas Muennighoff, Nouamane Tazi, Loïc Magne, Nils Reimers
extraction.rai:dataCollection: MTEB aggregates 58 datasets from 8 embedding tasks. Some datasets are reused from existing benchmarks like BEIR and SemEval (STS11-STS22). Other datasets are custom-made for MTEB using public APIs, such as arXiv, bioRxiv/medRxiv for clustering datasets, and Reddit/StackExchange posts.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Web API, Secondary Data analysis, Document analysis
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Raw data sources include: arXiv public API (https://arxiv.org/help/api/), bioRxiv/medRxiv API (https://api.biorxiv.org/), Reddit posts, StackExchange posts, 20 Newsgroups dataset, Amazon customer reviews, Tweets from SemEval 2015, BEIR benchmark datasets, SemEval datasets (STS12-STS22), Tatoeba, BUCC, and various other existing NLP datasets.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: For arXiv clustering, three types of splits are created: main category clustering, secondary category clustering within the same main category, and secondary category clustering across all categories. Subsets of labels are selected and articles are sampled from those labels.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: For S2S datasets the input text is the title of the paper; for P2P the input text is the concatenation of title and abstract. For arXiv, only the first category is used when multiple categories are given. For MSMARCO, the dev split is used instead of test following Thakur et al. (2021).
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Cluster labels are generated using categories given to papers by humans (e.g., arXiv, bioRxiv, medRxiv categories). For other datasets, existing human annotations from the source datasets are used (e.g., sentiment labels, intent labels, similarity scores).
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: MTEB uses versioning at dataset and software levels for reproducibility. JSON files corresponding to all results are made available. The benchmark welcomes dataset, task or metric contributions from the community via pull requests on GitHub. A public leaderboard is maintained on Hugging Face Hub.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The benchmark notes task imbalance — tasks in MTEB have different amounts of datasets with summarization consisting of only a single dataset. MTEB average scores are biased towards tasks with many datasets, notably retrieval, classification and clustering. Data contamination between MTEB datasets and model training datasets is acknowledged but not controlled for.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Limitations include: (1) Long document datasets are missing - longest datasets have only a few hundred words; (2) Task imbalance - summarization has only a single dataset; (3) Multilinguality is limited - retrieval and clustering are English-only; (4) Additional modalities (e.g., image) are not covered. The scale of experiments makes controlling for data contamination challenging.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: MTEB is intended for evaluating (testing) text embedding models across diverse tasks: Bitext mining, classification, clustering, pair classification, reranking, retrieval, STS and summarization. Use cases include selecting the right embedding model for practical applications and simplifying future embedding research.
